title: 邻居出远门前请你帮忙收信倒垃圾桶
titleEn: Helping your neighbour while he's away
scene: 周日下午，你在前院收衣服，隔壁的退休邻居 Graham 隔着矮墙跟你打招呼。他下周四要飞去布里斯班看女儿和刚出生的外孙，走两个多星期，想请你帮忙：周一晚上把垃圾桶推出去、收信、给后院的番茄浇水。Graham 人很热情，但说话快，满嘴 bin night、the green one、chock-a-block、a fortnight、no skin off my nose 这类说法。
你的目标：① 先寒暄、恭喜他，听懂他要走多久；② 把每件事问清楚：哪天放哪个桶、信放哪、怎么浇水、钥匙怎么给；③ 说明你自己哪个周末不在，交换电话，约好有事怎么联系。

facts.v: 这周四（19 号）出发，12 月 4 日（周五）回来，两周多
每周二早上收：红盖普通垃圾每周都放；黄盖回收和绿盖花园垃圾隔周轮换，周一晚上推出去
周三晚上 Graham 送备用钥匙过来，屋里有报警器，密码他发短信

vocab.zh: 放垃圾桶的那天晚上（收垃圾前一晚）
vocab.ex: Monday's bin night on our street, so the bins go out after dinner.

vocab.zh: 普通垃圾 / 可回收 / 花园有机垃圾桶（按盖子颜色叫）
vocab.ex: The yellow one goes out this week, and the green one next week.
Recycling only goes out every second week.

vocab.en: keep an eye on the place
vocab.ex: Would you mind keeping an eye on the place while I'm away?
I'll clear the letterbox every couple of days.
If the letterbox is chock-a-block, people know no one's home.
Just give the tomatoes a good soak every second evening.
The front garden's on a timer, so you don't need to worry about it.
I'll drop a spare key over on Wednesday night.
Punch in the code straight away so you don't set off the alarm.

vocab.en: it's no trouble / no skin off my nose
vocab.zh: 一点都不麻烦（后者更口语）
vocab.ex: Honestly, it's no trouble — I'm out there anyway.
Thanks heaps, I owe you one.

listening.en: Afternoon! Gorgeous day for it, eh? Have you got a sec?
listening.sound: Afternoon 前面省了 Good；eh 放句尾求认同，读“ay”；Have you got a sec 连读成 “hav-ya-got-a-sec”，sec = second，一小会儿
listening.zh: 下午好！天气真好啊，是吧？你有空吗？
listening.reply: Afternoon, Graham! Yeah, sure, what's up?

listening.en: I'm off up to Brissie Thursdee week — well, this Thursdee — to see our Sarah and the new bub.
listening.sound: Brissie = Brisbane；Thursdee 是 Thursday 的澳洲读法；bub = 小婴儿；off up to 只是“去（北边）”的意思
listening.zh: 我这周四要去布里斯班，看我女儿 Sarah 和刚出生的小宝宝。
listening.reply: Oh, congratulations! That's lovely news. How long are you going for?

listening.en: Bins go out Mondee night — red one every week, and it's the yellow one this week, then the green one the week after.
listening.sound: 信息量大：red every week，yellow 和 green 隔周轮换；Mondee = Monday
listening.zh: 周一晚上放垃圾桶——红的每周都放，这周放黄的，下周放绿的。
listening.reply: Sorry, could you say that again a bit slower? Red every week, and then yellow and green take turns?

listening.en: If it gets chockers, the junk mail's a dead giveaway that no one's home.
listening.sound: chockers = 塞满；a dead giveaway = 一眼就暴露
listening.zh: 信箱要是塞满了，那些广告单一看就知道家里没人。
listening.reply: Good point. I'll clear it every couple of days.

listening.en: Just chuck the mail on the kitchen bench — don't worry about sorting it.
listening.sound: chuck 在这里是“随手放”，不是“扔掉”；bench = 厨房台面
listening.zh: 信随手放厨房台面上就行，不用分。
listening.reply: No worries, I'll just pop it on the bench.

listening.en: Honestly, if it's too much of a hassle, just say so — I won't be offended.
listening.sound: hassle = 麻烦事；这是澳洲人的客气话，你回答“不麻烦”就好
listening.zh: 说真的，要是太麻烦你就直说，我不会介意。
listening.reply: Not at all, it's no trouble. That's what neighbours are for.

speech.topic: 我和邻居的相处：怎样从点头之交变成能互相帮忙的人
paragraphs: When I first moved to Australia, I didn't really know my neighbours. I would just smile and say hi when I saw them at the letterbox. I was a bit shy, and I was worried that my English wasn't good enough for a real chat.

Things changed when my next-door neighbour started talking to me about the weather and the bins. It sounds silly, but bin night was a great way to start. Every Monday evening we were both outside with our bins, so we had a few minutes to chat. Slowly I learnt about his family, his garden and his old job.

Now we help each other out. When he goes away, I clear his letterbox, put his bins out and water his tomatoes. When my family went on a holiday, he did the same for us, and he even mowed our front lawn without being asked. We also have each other's phone numbers, which makes me feel safer.

I think small things build trust. You don't need perfect English to be a good neighbour. You just need to be friendly, say yes when you can, and be clear when you can't. If I don't understand something, I simply ask him to say it again. He never minds.
My advice for new migrants is simple: start with a small chat at the letterbox or on bin night. Offer a little help, and accept help too. A good neighbour makes a new place feel like home.
speech.zh: 刚来澳洲时我和邻居只是点头之交，因为害羞、担心英语不好。后来隔壁邻居从天气和垃圾桶聊起，每周一晚上放垃圾桶成了我们聊天的机会，慢慢就熟了。现在我们互相帮忙：他出门我帮他收信、放桶、浇番茄；我们出门他也帮忙，甚至主动帮我们剪草。互存电话让我更有安全感。我觉得做好邻居不需要完美的英语，只要友好、能帮就帮、不能帮就说清楚，听不懂就请对方再说一遍。给新移民的建议：从信箱旁或放垃圾桶时的小聊天开始，愿意帮忙，也愿意接受帮助。

patterns.en: Would you mind ___ while I'm away?
patterns.zh: 我不在的时候，你介意帮我……吗？（请人帮忙）

patterns.en: No worries at all. Just to confirm, you want me to ___ on ___?
patterns.zh: 完全没问题。我确认一下，你是要我在……做……？

patterns.en: I'm happy to ___, but I won't be around on ___.
patterns.zh: 我很乐意……，不过……那天我不在。（答应但说明限制）

lines.en: Afternoon! Gorgeous day for it, eh? Have you got a sec?
lines.zh: 下午好！天气真好啊，是吧？你有空吗？

lines.en: Afternoon, Graham! Yeah, sure. What's up?
lines.zh: 下午好，Graham！有空，怎么了？

lines.en: Well, big news — our Sarah had the baby last week. A little girl. So I'm off up to Brissie this Thursdee to meet the new bub.
lines.zh: 是这样，大消息——我女儿 Sarah 上周生了，是个女孩。所以我这周四要去布里斯班看小宝宝。

lines.en: Oh, congratulations! That's lovely news. How long are you going for?
lines.zh: 哇，恭喜恭喜！太好了。你去多久？

lines.en: Just over a fortnight. Back on the fourth of December, all going well. Now, I hate to ask, but would you mind keeping an eye on the place while I'm gone?
lines.zh: 两个多星期吧。顺利的话十二月四号回来。我真不好意思开口，你介意我不在的时候帮忙照看一下房子吗？

lines.en: Of course, happy to help. What do you need me to do?
lines.zh: 当然，很乐意帮忙。需要我做什么？

lines.en: Righto, mainly the bins. Bins go out Mondee night — red one every week, and it's the yellow one this week, then the green one the week after, and so on.
lines.zh: 好嘞，主要是垃圾桶。周一晚上放——红的每周都放，这周放黄的，下周放绿的，就这样轮着来。

lines.en: Sorry, could you say that again a bit slower? So the red bin goes out every week, and the yellow and green ones take turns?
lines.zh: 不好意思，能说慢一点再讲一遍吗？就是红桶每周都放，黄桶和绿桶轮流放？

lines.en: Spot on. Every second week. Pickup's early Tuesdee morning, so if you could wheel them back in Tuesdee arvo, that'd be ace. Otherwise it's a bit of a giveaway.
lines.zh: 完全正确，隔周一次。周二一大早收，你周二下午帮我推回来就太好了，不然一看就知道没人在家。

lines.en: No worries. Monday night out, Tuesday afternoon back in. What about the mail?
lines.zh: 没问题。周一晚上推出去，周二下午推回来。那信件呢？

lines.en: Yeah, if you could clear the letterbox every couple of days. It gets chockers with junk mail, and that's a dead giveaway too. Just chuck it all on the kitchen bench — don't bother sorting it.
lines.zh: 嗯，麻烦你每隔一两天清一下信箱。广告单多得能塞满，那也是一眼就暴露。全放厨房台面上就行，不用分。

lines.en: Sure. Anything else? I saw your tomatoes out the back — they're looking great.
lines.zh: 好的。还有别的吗？我看你后院的番茄长得特别好。

lines.en: Ha, thanks. They're my pride and joy. The front garden's on a timer, so don't worry about that, but the tomatoes need a good soak every second evening, more if it's a stinker. Hose is round the side by the tap.
lines.zh: 哈，谢谢，那是我的宝贝。前院是定时浇水的，不用管，但番茄要隔一天傍晚浇透一次，要是特别热就多浇。水管在房子侧面水龙头旁边。

lines.en: Just to confirm, a stinker means a really hot day, right?
lines.zh: 我确认一下，stinker 是指特别热的天，对吧？

lines.en: That's the one. Anything over thirty-five, give them a drink every day if you can.
lines.zh: 对。超过三十五度的话，能的话就每天浇。

lines.en: Got it. One thing, though — I'm happy to do all that, but we're away the weekend of the twenty-ninth. We're going down to Victor Harbor.
lines.zh: 明白。不过有一点——我很乐意做这些，但二十九号那个周末我们不在，要去 Victor Harbor。

lines.en: Oh, no dramas at all. A couple of days won't hurt. I'll ask Bev across the road to cover that weekend. It's no skin off her nose, she's always out walking the dog.
lines.zh: 哦，完全没关系，两天没事的。那个周末我请对面的 Bev 帮忙，对她来说一点不麻烦，她总在外面遛狗。

lines.en: Great. How will I get in, if I need to?
lines.zh: 太好了。如果我需要进屋，怎么进？

lines.en: I'll drop a spare key over Wednesdee night. There's an alarm, mind you — the keypad's just inside the front door. I'll text you the code so I don't forget it myself.
lines.zh: 我周三晚上把备用钥匙送过来。不过有报警器——按键板就在前门进去那儿。我把密码短信发给你，免得我自己忘了。

lines.en: Perfect. Do you have my number? It's 0491 570 147.
lines.zh: 好的。你有我的电话吗？是 0491 570 147。

lines.en: Hang on, let me grab my phone... 0491 570 147. Done. I'll send you a text now so you've got mine. If anything goes pear-shaped, just give us a bell.
lines.zh: 等一下，我拿手机……0491 570 147，存好了。我现在给你发条短信，你就有我的号了。要是出了什么岔子，给我打电话就行。

lines.en: Will do. And if anything comes up, I'll send you a photo as well.
lines.zh: 好的。万一有什么情况，我也会拍照发给你。

lines.en: You're a legend. Honestly, if it's too much of a hassle, just say so — I won't be offended.
lines.zh: 你真是太好了。说真的，要是太麻烦你就直说，我不会介意。

lines.en: Not at all, it's no trouble. That's what neighbours are for. Have a great trip, and give the baby a cuddle from us.
lines.zh: 一点也不麻烦，邻居就是互相帮忙的嘛。祝你旅途愉快，替我们抱抱小宝宝。

lines.en: Will do. Thanks heaps, I owe you one. I'll bring you back something from Queensland — a mango or two, at least!
lines.zh: 一定。太感谢了，欠你个人情。我从昆士兰给你带点东西回来——起码带几个芒果！

rescue.en: Sorry, could you say that again a bit slower?
rescue.zh: 不好意思，能说慢一点再讲一遍吗？

rescue.en: Sorry, what do you mean by ___?
Just to confirm, you want me to ___ on ___, right?
rescue.zh: 我确认一下，你是要我在……做……，对吗？

rescue.en: Could you write that down for me, or text it to me?
rescue.zh: 能帮我写下来，或者发短信给我吗？

rescue.en: Which one is that again — the yellow lid or the green lid?
rescue.zh: 再说一下是哪个——黄盖的还是绿盖的？

checklist: 我能用 Congratulations! / How long are you going for? 自然地寒暄
我能听懂 bin night、red one every week、every second week，并说出哪天放哪个桶
我能听懂 chockers、a dead giveaway、chuck it on the bench，知道信件怎么处理
我能用 Just to confirm... 确认 stinker、give them a good soak 这类不熟的说法
我能礼貌说明自己哪个周末不在，而不是什么都直接答应
我和邻居交换了电话，约好钥匙、报警器密码和有事怎么联系
